CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in bilateral hands

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 60-year-old right-handed male referred for evaluation of bilateral numbness and tingling. Symptoms began several weeks ago and became more noticeable after bilateral wrist fractures sustained in a motor vehicle accident in December 2025. The right wrist was fractured more severely than the left. During the same accident, patient sustained a head contusion. Following healing of the fractures, patient noted worsening of tingling and numbness, with significant progression over the past month. Patient reports associated mild neck stiffness since the head injury. He currently wears wrist splints bilaterally, with the right wrist being the primary site of symptoms.

Patient describes symptoms on the right as extending from the middle and ring fingers up the forearm, and on the left from the pinky and ring finger. The primary complaint is soreness with occasional throbbing and associated weakness, particularly with hand use. Tingling is more pronounced during pain episodes and becomes duller when pain improves. Symptoms occur predominantly at night with fluctuation throughout the day. Patient denies complete sensory loss but reports the hands may be less sensitive than normal. He was prescribed nerve pain medication but reports inconsistent compliance.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: Fatigue and weight gain. Gastrointestinal: Excessive appetite and bloating. HEENT: Eye floaters. Cardiovascular: Shortness of breath and leg swelling. Endocrine: Persistent hunger. Skin: Nail bed changes, dryness, and itching. Musculoskeletal: History of gout and muscle pain. All other systems reviewed and negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Bilateral wrist fractures (December 2025, secondary to motor vehicle accident)
2. Head contusion (motor vehicle accident)
3. Prediabetes (controlled with dietary modification)
4. Hypertension
5. Anxiety disorder

MEDICATIONS
1. Coreg (for hypertension)
2. Lexapro (for anxiety)
3. Nerve pain medication (prescribed; patient reports inconsistent use)

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is right-handed. History of motor vehicle accident in December 2025. Additional social history not documented at this visit.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurologic examination: Sensation intact globally except for diminished pin prick sensation in the 3rd and 4th fingers of the right hand and decreased sensation in the 4th and 5th fingers of the left hand. Reflexes 1+ and symmetric in upper extremities; 2+ at knees; bilateral downgoing toes. Tinel sign positive at both wrists and both elbows. Remainder of neurologic exam normal. General physical examination: Remainder of exam normal.

RESULTS
Neurologic examination as documented above.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, likely secondary to prior bilateral wrist trauma from motor vehicle accident. Differential diagnosis includes bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome, though clinical presentation is more consistent with carpal tunnel syndrome.

Plan:
1. Schedule electromyography (EMG) testing to measure nerve responsiveness and precisely identify the location of nerve irritation
2. Follow-up appointment after EMG testing is completed
3. If symptoms persist, consider referral to hand surgery clinic for steroid injections or carpal tunnel release surgery, or alternatively referral to orthopedic surgery for similar treatment options
4. Continue bilateral wrist splints
5. Patient counseled to take prescribed nerve pain medication consistently
